findings.summary: smoke:liquify fails ~23% of runs on an unmodified tree, at three different assertions — so it cannot distinguish a regression from its own noise.
findings.rationale: CLAIM: 3 failures in 13 consecutive clean runs at HEAD — '[1] liquify canvas missing', '[3] grab handle did not change the render', '[4] physics frame went blank'. EVIDENCE: every green run produces byte-identical numbers (push delta 3.77, grab delta 21.03, physics variety 51), so the underlying render is deterministic and the variance is in timing, not math. The smoke uses one-shot waitForTimeouts before every readback and has NEITHER the dep-optimize retry loop NOR the Vite dual-instance detector that its sibling smoke-gx-geom-handles.mts carries — and gx-handles was 13/13 clean here and goes red on a real break. preserveDrawingBuffer is true on both the liquify and compositor contexts, so this is not the classic WebGL readback race. OPTIONS: (a) port the retry loop + dual-instance guard from smoke-gx-geom-handles.mts and replace fixed waits with polling until the signature stabilises — cheap, and the sibling is a proven template; (b) treat '[4] physics frame went blank' as a possible real liquify divergence and instrument it before touching the smoke — the LiquifyMesh unit test asserts finiteness and boundedness over 600 frames and passes, which argues against a blowup but does not cover the GL display path; (c) leave it and rely on re-running. RECOMMENDATION: (a), escalating to (b) only if a hardened smoke still goes blank. Not applied because a guard rewrite is unreviewed code and there was no way to run enough post-change trials on a tree two other auditors were editing to beat a 23% baseline statistically. The flakiness IS now documented in .claude/rules/sibling-apps.md so nobody reads a red run as a regression in the meantime.

findings.summary: Two structural blind spots in the guard-citation checker, both found by falsification, both invisible from its output.
findings.rationale: CLAIM 1 — rule-granularity: it matches guards against a rule's ENTIRE paths: set, so in a multi-app rule any guard touching any one app satisfies every row. Proved by moving npm run smoke:fluid-toy into sibling-apps.md's gradient-explorer row: output identical, still 4 issues. That rule scopes five apps and its own prose warns 'running a fluid-toy smoke proves nothing about mesh-export' — precisely the class it cannot see. CLAIM 2 — chained scripts: it resolves an npm script by its FIRST command only. test:palette is sixteen tsx invocations joined by &&; citing it produced a FALSE 5th issue naming debug/test-palette-stopfit.mts, having never reached debug/test-liquify-mesh.mts, the link that does cover the rule's files. OPTIONS: (a) split multi-app rules into one rule per app so path-granularity matches citation-granularity; (b) teach the checker to parse guards per table row / per section heading; (c) teach it to union the reachable sets of every &&-joined command in a script — small, and strictly removes false positives; (d) leave it and hand-check. RECOMMENDATION: (c) first (cheapest, removes a false-positive class outright), then (b). This is the run's own guard-health tooling and outside this subsystem, so nothing was changed in it — only sibling-apps.md now states the limitation. CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY: the a03-tutorial auditor falsified smoke:undo against engine/plugins/tutorial/triggers.ts the same cycle and found it cannot fail there, while check:rule-guards reports engine-plugins.md as clean — the same blind spot, reached from the opposite end of the tree.

findings.summary: The sole guard for ADR-0065/0066 deep-zoom glitch-freedom is filed under gradient-explorer and could not be baselined; the rule that owns deep zoom cites three smokes that check:rule-guards says cannot fail.
findings.rationale: CLAIM: grep -rn gx-fractal-glitch .claude/rules/ returns exactly one hit — sibling-apps.md's gradient-explorer row. It genuinely reaches gradient-explorer code (boots gradient-explorer.html, mounts the fullscreen overlay, drives fullscreen/modes/fractalMode.tsx as an ownCanvas mode), so the citation is defensible. But its ASSERTIONS are entirely deep-zoom contracts — LA-on vs LA-off central colour distribution, auto-reference relocation, ADR-0066 periodic-nucleus adoption — and gmt-formulas-and-graph.md, which owns that area, does not cite it, while the three deep-zoom smokes it does cite are 3 of the 4 miscitations check:rule-guards reports. EVIDENCE on health: two attempts, both killed at the third view by a Vite full-reload from concurrent auditors; every assertion reached passed. OPTIONS: (a) also cite it from gmt-formulas-and-graph.md so a deep-zoom change surfaces the one guard that tests deep zoom — additive, no risk; (b) leave it and let the deep-zoom rule's citations get fixed independently. RECOMMENDATION: (a), and give this smoke a quiet tree in the guard sweep — it needs ~8 uninterrupted minutes and is the only ADR-0065/0066 coverage in the repo. Not applied because gmt-formulas-and-graph.md belongs to another subsystem and its four known miscitations were explicitly out of remit.
